issues.legal_issue: Rules governing the appointment of arbitrators and the conduct of arbitration proceedings fall within the authority to make rules for those subjects.
material_facts: The challenged rules provided a procedure for appointing an arbitrator when objectors failed to elect one.
Other challenged rules regulated the proceedings before the arbitrators.
The rule-making authority extended to the mode of appointment of arbitrators and the regulation of their proceedings.
The rules were made under that rule-making authority.
issues.conclusion: The challenged rules were within the rule-making authority and were not ultra vires.
issues.legal_principle: Section 137(3a) of the Calcutta Improvement Act, 1911 authorized rules concerning the appointment of arbitrators and the regulation of proceedings under section 78C. Section 86 concerned the purposes of Chapter V and did not supply the relevant authority for provisions in Chapter IV. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: delegated_rule_challenge and (rule_addresses_arbitrator_appointment or rule_addresses_arbitration_procedure) and enabling_authority_covers_rule_subject

predicates.delegated_rule_challenge: A proceeding challenges rules made by a public authority as exceeding the authority to make them.
predicates.rule_addresses_arbitrator_appointment: The challenged rule provides a method for appointing an arbitrator.
predicates.rule_addresses_arbitration_procedure: The challenged rule regulates the conduct of arbitration proceedings.
predicates.enabling_authority_covers_rule_subject: The authority to make rules expressly covers the subject addressed by the challenged rule.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns delegated rules and the rules address arbitrator appointment or procedure within subjects covered by the enabling authority, the rules fall within that authority.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory framework for charging a betterment fee does not involve excessive delegation when the selection of scheme areas is guided, affected owners have opportunities to object, and disputed assessments are independently reviewable.
material_facts: The framework limited schemes to public improvement purposes, including creating or improving streets and traffic facilities.
A scheme required approval by the State Government, which could modify or refuse it.
Affected owners could object to the proposed recovery of a fee and be heard, and the scheme could be modified to exclude land.
The fee depended on an increase in land value attributable to the scheme, which the assessing body had to determine objectively.
An owner who disputed the assessment could have the matter determined by independent arbitrators.
issues.conclusion: The provisions governing betterment fees were not invalid for excessive delegation of legislative power.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 39 and 78A to 78G of the Calcutta Improvement Act, 1911 supplied the purposes and framework for schemes and betterment fees. The Court considered the statutory guidance, government sanction, opportunities to object, objective assessment of increased land value, and review by independent arbitrators sufficient to prevent arbitrary or uncontrolled exercise of delegated power. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: excessive_delegation_challenge and scheme_area_has_guided_public_purposes and scheme_requires_government_review and affected_owners_can_object_and_be_heard and fee_depends_on_actual_land_value_increase and disputed_assessment_has_independent_review

predicates.excessive_delegation_challenge: A proceeding challenges a statutory framework for imposing a betterment fee as an excessive delegation of legislative power.
predicates.scheme_area_has_guided_public_purposes: The area included in a public improvement scheme is selected by reference to stated improvement purposes.
predicates.scheme_requires_government_review: A public authority other than the scheme-making body can review, modify, or refuse the scheme.
predicates.affected_owners_can_object_and_be_heard: Owners affected by a proposed fee can object and have their reasons considered at a hearing.
predicates.fee_depends_on_actual_land_value_increas: The fee is linked to an increase in land value caused by the improvement scheme.
predicates.disputed_assessment_has_independent_revi: An owner disputing the assessment can obtain a determination from independent decision-makers.

issues.definition: When an excessive-delegation challenge concerns a betterment-fee framework, and the scheme is guided and reviewed, owners can object, the fee depends on actual value increase, and disputed assessments receive independent review, the framework is not invalid for excessive delegation.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory betterment-fee framework does not violate equal protection when its operation is guided and includes safeguards against arbitrary assessments.
material_facts: The framework confined schemes to stated public improvement purposes and required State Government sanction.
Affected owners could object to the proposed fee and be heard.
The fee was tied to an objectively determined increase in land value attributable to the scheme.
Owners could refer disputed assessments to independent arbitrators.
issues.conclusion: The challenge under Article 14 failed because it was another facet of the unsuccessful excessive-delegation challenge.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 of the Constitution was considered in connection with sections 78A to 78G of the Calcutta Improvement Act, 1911. The Court treated the equality challenge as another facet of the excessive-delegation challenge and relied on the framework's guidance and safeguards against arbitrary decisions. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: equal_protection_challenge_to_betterment_framework and scheme_area_has_guided_public_purposes and scheme_requires_government_review and affected_owners_can_object_and_be_heard and fee_depends_on_actual_land_value_increase and disputed_assessment_has_independent_review

predicates.equal_protection_challenge_to_betterment: A proceeding challenges a betterment-fee framework as unequal or arbitrary.
predicates.scheme_area_has_guided_public_purposes: The area included in a public improvement scheme is selected by reference to stated improvement purposes.
predicates.scheme_requires_government_review: A public authority other than the scheme-making body can review, modify, or refuse the scheme.
predicates.affected_owners_can_object_and_be_heard: Owners affected by a proposed fee can object and have their reasons considered at a hearing.
predicates.fee_depends_on_actual_land_value_increas: The fee is linked to an increase in land value caused by the improvement scheme.
predicates.disputed_assessment_has_independent_revi: An owner disputing the assessment can obtain a determination from independent decision-makers.

issues.definition: When an equal-protection challenge concerns a betterment-fee framework whose scheme is guided and reviewed, whose affected owners can object, whose fee depends on actual value increase, and whose disputed assessments receive independent review, the framework does not violate equal protection.
